entry.title: Brakeza3D 0.26.10 released!
entry.summary: Brakeza3D 0.26.10 is here! This release is all about performance and polish: a reworked renderer
entry.content:
Brakeza3D 0.26.10 is here! This release is all about performance and polish: a reworked renderer with instancing and shared GPU geometry, emissive materials, a brand-new audio backend, faster async loading, a much more capable UI system, path costs for pathfinding, and command-line parameters for automated runs.

Download for Linux and Windows:

  • https://github.com/rzeronte/brakeza3d/releases/tag/0.26.10
  • https://brakeza.com/downloads

✨ What's New​

Rendering Performance Overhaul​

The deferred renderer has been profiled and optimized end to end. Scenes with many copies of the same model are now dramatically cheaper.

  • Shared GPU geometry — every Mesh3D / Mesh3DAnimation created from the same model file shares its vertex buffers, with deduplicated index buffers
  • Instancing — an opaque render queue groups objects by model and draws them instanced in the G-Buffer, shadow and picking passes. Animated models too: bones are skinned in the vertex shader from a bone-matrix texture buffer
  • Shadow caster culling — each light only renders the casters inside its own frustum
  • State caches — FBO/program bind cache and a shared GL render-state cache remove redundant state changes; projection and view travel in a single CameraBlock uniform buffer

Emissive Materials​

Mesh3D objects can now glow with their own color, ignoring scene lighting: screens, neon signs, lamps, magic effects. Emission is off by default and adds no cost to scenes that do not use it.

local sign = Brakeza:getObjectByName("neon_sign")
sign:setEmissionEnabled(true)
sign:setEmissionIntensity(0.8)   -- 0 = lit normally, 1 = full self-illumination

Available in the object inspector, saved in scene files and fully scriptable.

New Audio Backend: miniaudio​

SDL2_mixer has been replaced by miniaudio, bundled as a single header — one dependency less to install on Linux.

  • Same Lua API as before (playSound, channels, Sound3D, ambience volume...)
  • WAV, MP3 and FLAC support, also for positional Sound3D sources
  • New setChannelPitch(channel, pitch) for engine RPM, Doppler and similar effects

Faster Async Loading​

  • Per-file load locks in the resource caches: the same file is never loaded twice in parallel
  • The compute thread pool is sized from the CPU core count
  • Deferrable jobs: work that has to wait no longer blocks a worker thread
  • Animated billboards get their own texture cache
  • Brakeza:getPendingJobsCount() and Brakeza:cancelPendingJobs() to drive loading screens and clean restarts; Components:Render():PreloadImage2D(path) warms up images before they are shown

UI System Upgrades​

The widget system takes a big step forward:

FeatureDetail
Fonts per widget and per elementAny .ttf / .otf; nested widgets inherit the parent's font
Word-wrapped textwrap, w, maxLines and lineSpacing on text elements
9-slice backgroundsbgSlice: frames whose corners keep their size when the panel is resized
Scrollable listsNew scroll element type
Pagers on toparrayPagerTop places a long list's pager above it
Resolution-aware textsetUIDesignResolution(w, h) and per-widget refHeight scale text with the window
New Lua helpersgetWidgetSize, invalidateWidget, invalidateAllWidgets, isUIScrollHovered

The UI Manager editor window gained the matching controls (font pickers, grouped sections...).

Related rendering helpers:

  • drawFillSubmesh(obj, submesh, r, g, b, a) — translucent highlight over a single submesh
  • TextWriter:measureTextWidthAtlas(text, scale) — measure batched atlas text to center or align it; atlas text now honors its tint color and blends correctly

Pathfinding — Path Costs​

Grid3D cells can now have a traversal cost. A* prefers cheaper cells, so units can favour sidewalks over roads or avoid dangerous areas without blocking them:

local grid = mesh:getGrid3D()
grid:fillCostFromImage("../assets/nav/roads.png", 128, 4.0)   -- roads cost 4
grid:setCellsCost({ 10, 12, 11, 12 }, 10.0)                   -- a temporary danger zone
print(grid:getCellCost(10, 12))

Grid world coordinates are now derived from the grid bounds.

Command-Line Parameters & Automation​

Projects can declare their own parameters and receive them from the command line — ideal for test scenarios, CI and benchmarks:

> brakeza3d.exe -p MyGame.json --set level=forest --set godMode=true --exit-after 300
  • --set key=value — passed to the project, declared in its cli_params (name, type, default)
  • --exit-after N — safety watchdog for headless runs
  • Brakeza:getCliParam(name) reads a parameter with its declared type
  • Brakeza:requestExit(code) closes the app with a process exit code

Scripting API Additions​

APIDescription
Brakeza:getDeltaTimeMS()Frame time in milliseconds (getDeltaTimeMicro() now really returns microseconds)
Brakeza:getImage3DAnimationByName()Typed access to animated billboards
BillboardAnimation:setTowardsCamera / setSize / setRenderFBFlat ground sprites, runtime resizing, render layer
Mesh3D:getModelFile() / getDiffuseTextureFile(i)Inspect the model and per-submesh textures
Input:isMouseInWindow()Know when the cursor leaves the window
ParticlesContext.PARTICLE_SIZE_SCALEParticle size multiplier

Profiler — Render Detail​

The Profiler adds exact per-frame draw call and triangle counters, CPU and real GPU time per render pass (GPU queries are optional, zero overhead when off), rolling history with median/P95/P99, and CSV export to compare a scene before and after an optimization.

Editor & Platform​

  • Scene badge in the project panel
  • Windows: the application icon is embedded in the executable (taskbar icon from the first frame)
  • New minimal UITest demo scene (UIWidgetsDemo.lua) showing a plain widget, a nested widget and an array with the sample widgets in assets/ui/

Bug Fixes​

  • Texture unit helpers only handled units 0–5 (higher units were bound onto the previous one)
  • UI widget editor now saves arrayPrefix
  • Black scene after a window resize (VAO name reuse in ground decals)
  • VRAM leak when destroying custom code shaders
  • Outline fill pass inheriting instancing flags
  • Editor grid disappearing
  • Two use-after-free crashes
  • Camera up vector computed from its own rotation

Documentation​

  • UI Widgets — new dedicated page: JSON format, element types, buttons, nested widgets, lists and pagination, scroll areas, 9-slice backgrounds, text scaling and the UI Manager editor
  • 3D Objects — Mesh3D model/texture methods, emission, shared geometry and instancing, animated billboards
  • Grid3D — movement costs
  • Scripting introduction — command-line parameters (--set, cli_params, --exit-after), requestExit, async loading helpers
  • Sound — miniaudio backend, supported formats, setChannelPitch
  • Text System — custom fonts with the glyph atlas, batched text and measureTextWidthAtlas
  • Editor — Profiler counters, GPU timing and CSV export
  • Download and Install — build from source updated: new Windows libraries package for 0.26.10 (no SDL2_mixer, exact MinGW build it needs) and the FFmpeg development packages on Linux

Thanks for testing Brakeza3D and sharing feedback ❤️

entry.title: Brakeza3D 0.26.8 released!
entry.summary: Brakeza3D 0.26.8 is here! This release is packed with major new features: a full positional audio system, multi-scene support, video playback, a new Swarm entity, multi-selection across editor and scripting, and a large batch of rendering, physics, and editor improvements.
entry.content:
Brakeza3D 0.26.8 is here! This release is packed with major new features: a full positional audio system, multi-scene support, video playback, a new Swarm entity, multi-selection across editor and scripting, and a large batch of rendering, physics, and editor improvements.

Download for Linux and Windows:

  • https://github.com/rzeronte/brakeza3d/releases/tag/0.26.8
  • https://brakeza.com/downloads

✨ What's New​

Sound3D — Positional Audio System​

A brand-new Sound3D scene object brings distance-based volume attenuation to the engine. Place ambient sounds anywhere in the world and let the engine handle volume falloff automatically based on the camera's distance.

  • Full inner/outer radius model: full volume inside innerRadius, linear fade to silence at outerRadius
  • Can be placed in the editor, saved in scene files, or created from Lua with ObjectFactory.Sound3D()
  • Global ambience volume — Components:Sound():setAmbienceVolume(percent) scales all Sound3D sources simultaneously, perfect for ducking world sounds during menus or cutscenes
  • Zone music crossfade: overlapping outer radii produce natural transitions with zero scripting
  • Background music mode: set innerRadius to a very large value for a non-positional track
local snd = ObjectFactory.Sound3D(
    "../assets/sounds/forest_ambient.wav",
    Vertex3D.new(0, 0, 0), 20, 80, 100
)
snd:setSoundLoop(true)
Brakeza:addObject3D(snd, "forest_ambient")

Multi-Scene System​

Scenes can now be loaded, shown, and hidden independently at runtime. Multiple scenes can coexist and be toggled without losing their state.

  • Brakeza:loadScene(path) / Brakeza:showScene(name) / Brakeza:hideScene(name)
  • Scene shader chains are properly saved and restored when a scene is hidden and re-shown — shaders that were disabled before hiding stay disabled on restore
  • Enables interior/exterior streaming: load interior scene, hide exterior, restore on exit

Video Player in Image2D​

Image2D objects can now play back video files directly inside the engine. Use the editor or Lua to assign a video source and control playback.

Swarm Entity​

A new Swarm object type for managing large groups of simple elements (particles, foliage, crowds) as a single scene node. Registered in the full serialization pipeline with editor inspector support.

Multi-Selection — Editor & Scripting​

Select multiple objects simultaneously in the viewport and operate on them as a group.

  • Ctrl + Left Click — toggle an object into/out of the current selection group
  • Ctrl + Left Drag — rectangle-select all objects inside the drawn area
  • Full scripting access via the new SelectionManager (extracted from ComponentRender), exposable to Lua
  • MultiSelectionDemo.lua updated with working examples

Rendering — Blob Shadows & Ground Circles​

Two new lightweight render primitives for real-time ground projection effects:

  • Blob shadows — circular soft-shadow decals projected onto the ground beneath objects
  • Ground circles — configurable radius/color rings for selection indicators, AoE zones, and UI feedback

Both are registered as GUI addons and fully scriptable from Lua.

Collider System Improvements​

  • Debug draw — visualize collision shapes in the viewport at runtime
  • Contact points — query per-frame collision contact data from Lua
  • resetColliderRotation() — snap a body's orientation back to identity without repositioning
  • Ghost body fix — ghost objects no longer interfere with dynamic simulation incorrectly
  • ColliderGUI refactored into its own standalone panel

Shadow Pass Optimization​

The shadow pass now skips meshes and scene regions that cannot cast shadows into the current light frustum, reducing GPU draw calls significantly in larger scenes.

Editor Improvements​

FeatureDetail
Solo window toggleFocus a single dockable panel, hiding the rest
Layout restoreLayouts are saved and restored across sessions
forceReloadLayoutForce-rebuild the dock layout from the current preset
`Ctrl + `` shortcutQuick toggle between CODING and DEFAULT layouts
Snap camera viewsInsert (front), Home (top), Page Up (side) — snaps camera to selected object

UIManager Improvements​

  • bgColor arrays: per-widget background color now accepts RGBA arrays in JSON
  • cacheable: false flag — bypass FBO caching for widgets that update position or alpha every frame (e.g. world-space unit overlays)
  • New scripting methods exposed: setWidgetAlpha, setWidgetPosition, showWidget, hideWidget, and more

TextWriter​

  • Tint color — writeTextAtlasCache now accepts a tint color parameter, enabling colored cached text without recreating the atlas
  • flushTextBatch() flushes the colored glyph batch correctly

Sound System — Per-Channel Control​

New Lua API for fine-grained channel control:

-- Pitch/frequency (engine RPM simulation, Doppler)
Components:Sound():setChannelFrequency(channel, freq)

-- Per-channel volume (independent of global setSoundsVolume)
Components:Sound():setChannelVolume(channel, vol)

-- 3D spatialization via angle + distance
Components:Sound():setChannelPosition(channel, angle, distance)

-- Query channel state
Components:Sound():isChannelPlaying(channel)
Components:Sound():isSoundPlaying("label")

Tools​

  • fbx_bounds.py — Python tool to extract vertex bounds from FBX files, useful for computing exact mesh positions after Blender export

Documentation​

Major documentation additions:

  • Sound3D — new dedicated API page covering positional audio, zone crossfade, ambience volume, and Lua methods
  • Sound System — expanded with per-channel control, isSoundPlaying, and setAmbienceVolume
  • Components API — UIManager widget system documented (9 methods)
  • 3D Objects — Image3DAnimation360 section added
  • Shaders System — pipeline order and execution steps documented
  • Keyboard Shortcuts — snap camera keys (Insert / Home / Page Up) added

Profiler — Expanded Diagnostics​

The built-in ImGui profiler gained a large set of new panels, turning it into a full runtime diagnostics tool:

PanelWhat it shows
Frame TimePer-frame ms plot with 120-frame rolling history
ComponentsPer-component pre/update/post timing breakdown with sparklines
Script DetailPer-Lua-script timing, toggled independently
CachesLive entry counts and memory usage for Image, Model, Animation, Script, and Scene caches
Frame BuffersAll active FBOs with their color/depth attachments and dimensions
OpenGL StatusCurrent GL state: bound program, bound FBO, active texture units, FBO/program switch counters per frame
Post-Processing ChainEnabled/disabled status and execution order of every scene shader in the chain
Thread PoolsActive tasks, pending tasks, pending callbacks, total processed, and a 120-frame throughput sparkline per pool
CollidersRuntime list of active physics bodies with mode, group, and AABB
System MemoryTotal and free RAM on Windows, Linux, and macOS via native OS APIs

FBO and GL program switch counters are incremented at the call site throughout the render pipeline, giving exact per-frame context switch counts with no estimation.

Bug Fixes & Maintenance​

  • Fixed GCC warnings in debug mode across multiple translation units
  • Fixed X11 + NVIDIA OpenGL window creation on Linux
  • Fixed Image2D size/position regression
  • Fixed bad dynamic_cast in core components
  • Removed RTS-specific demo widgets from engine examples, keeping only generic ones
  • Debian build setup scripts updated

This release marks a significant step forward in audio, scene management, and editor workflow. Thanks for testing Brakeza3D and sharing feedback ❤️

entry.title: Thanks and Roadmap!
entry.content:
First of all, thank you.

I want to take a moment to thank everyone who has emailed me and shown so much interest after the latest video about the Brakeza3D 0.26.2 release. The response from the community has been incredibly positive and motivating, and it truly means a lot to see so many people interested, testing the engine, and asking how they can use it or contribute.

About the roadmap​

One of the questions that keeps coming up in messages is:

What is the project's roadmap?

The answer is clear and honest:
The current priority is not to add lots of new features, but to stabilize and consolidate the project.

The main focus right now is:

  • Stabilizing the engine
  • Improving internal consistency
  • Exposing 100% of the engine’s functionality to LUA
  • Properly documenting that API

At the moment, the LUA API is still limited, and before expanding the engine with new capabilities, I want to make sure everything that already exists is:

  • accessible
  • stable
  • documented
  • maintainable

This step is essential to make the project truly usable in the long term.

Priorities for the coming months​

The priority order will be:

  1. Bug fixing
  2. Documenting the LUA API and the C++ core
  3. Desired features
  4. Long-term features

This order is intentional. An engine with many features but poor stability or documentation ends up being frustrating for users. I prefer building a solid foundation before accelerating development.

Desired features (mid-term)​

These are some improvements planned that will be implemented progressively:

  • Improve user experience in the interface
  • Enable geometry streaming for Mesh3D objects
  • Add a basic version of node-based geometry shaders

Many of these ideas come directly from community feedback, which helps a lot when deciding what actually brings value.

Long-term features (or subject to reconsideration)​

There are also deeper evolution paths that require analysis and experimentation before any decision is made:

  • Decouple OpenGL / Create a Vulkan backend
  • Explore alternative scripting language options
  • Change the project's license type

These decisions affect the architecture, philosophy, and long-term direction of the engine, so they will be evaluated carefully and with community feedback.

Thanks again​

To close, I want to repeat the most important thing:
thank you for the interest, feedback, and support.

This project keeps moving forward thanks to you.

Let’s keep going 🚀

entry.title: Brakeza3D 0.26.2 released!
entry.content:
Brakeza3D 0.26.2 is now available! 🚀
This release focuses on editor usability, shader workflow improvements, scripting enhancements, and major internal cleanup.

Download for Linux and Windows:

  • https://github.com/rzeronte/brakeza3d/releases/tag/0.26.2
  • https://brakeza.com/downloads

✨ What’s New​

Rendering & Shaders​

  • Multiple Mesh3DShaderChain fixes
  • Improved Shader Node Editor processing
  • New internal texture nodes

Editor & UX​

  • Native toolbar with updated icons and colors
  • Script/shader editor improvements
  • Documented shortcuts + “Close all tabs” button
  • Custom project tree widgets

Assets & Projects​

  • Massive cleanup of scenes and demos
  • Sound asset integration
  • Unified file browser (scenes, scripts, projects)
  • Improved project setup and editable metadata

Scripting & Lua​

  • Bullet functions exposed to Lua
  • Better ComponentScripting workflow
  • New tutorials and expanded example scripts
  • Script-controlled sound volume
  • New Clean() function for selective cleanup

Docs & Maintenance​

  • Continuous documentation updates
  • Linux CMake fixes
  • Memory management improvements
  • ImGui style balancing
  • Extensive .gitignore cleanup

This release brings a cleaner foundation and a smoother workflow across the engine and editor.

Thanks to everyone testing Brakeza3D and providing feedback ❤️

entry.title: Assets Hub Alpha released!
entry.content:
Assets Hub Alpha Released 🚀​

We’re excited to announce the alpha release of Assets Hub, a new platform designed to expand and strengthen the Brakeza3D ecosystem.

Assets Hub is an integrated portal where the community can share, discover, and reuse scripts and shaders created by other Brakeza3D users. The main goal is to encourage collaboration, learning, and faster development through high-quality community-driven resources.

Deep Integration with Brakeza3D​

Assets Hub is directly integrated into the Brakeza3D engine. The engine now includes a built-in client that allows users to:

  • Log in to their Assets Hub account
  • Browse community-created assets
  • Vote and rate resources
  • Download scripts and shaders created by third parties

All of this happens without leaving the engine, keeping the workflow fast and seamless.

Web Portal for Asset Management​

Assets Hub is also available as a web platform at:

https://hub.brakeza.com/

From the web interface, creators can upload, update, and manage their assets, making it easy to maintain and showcase their contributions to the community.

Alpha Status​

Assets Hub is currently in alpha, which means it is still under active development. Features, workflows, and APIs may change in the coming weeks as we iterate based on feedback.

This early stage is a great opportunity for the community to test the platform and help shape its future.

Free and Ad-Free​

Assets Hub is a free service, with no advertisements and no hidden costs. It is built to support the Brakeza3D community and promote open sharing and collaboration.

entry.title: Welcome to Brakeza3D!
entry.summary: The Brakeza3D website has been completely relaunched as a site dedicated to providing solid and up-to-date documentation.
entry.content:
The Brakeza3D website has been completely relaunched as a site dedicated to providing solid and up-to-date documentation.

We’ve redesigned the website from the ground up to make it easier for developers to find tutorials, API references, download links, and more.

The goal is to help both new and experienced users get the most out of the Brakeza3D engine efficiently.

Stay tuned for updates, tutorials, and examples that will guide you in creating amazing 2D and 3D games with Brakeza3D!.
